whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Agentforce Specialist exam?

personas.label: Salesforce administrators
personas.description: You understand Salesforce configuration and want to learn how Agentforce agents fit into that environment.

personas.label: Automation practitioners
personas.description: You build flows or other automations and want to extend your skills to agent topics, actions, prompts, and testing.

personas.label: Consultants and architects
personas.description: You design Salesforce solutions and want to demonstrate your ability to plan and configure Agentforce use cases.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Agentforce Specialist exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers Agentforce configuration and assumes familiarity with Salesforce. Salesforce recommends relevant hands-on experience, but the experience guidance is not a prerequisite.
bullets: Exam length: 60 scored multiple-choice questions, with up to five unscored questions, in 105 minutes.
No required prerequisite: Platform Administrator and Platform App Builder are recommended credentials, not entry requirements.
Practical preparation: The exam guide recommends experience with Agent Builder, Prompt Builder, Data 360, Testing Center, and deployment from sandbox to production.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use the official exam outline to plan your study. Where possible, build and test agents in a suitable environment, then practice explaining why each topic, action, grounding source, and escalation path fits its use case.

examFormat.heading: Agentforce Specialist exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored and can be taken online or in person. Review the current official guide for booking and delivery details.
bestWayToPass: Practice with Agent Builder: Configure topics and actions, then test how the agent handles common requests and escalation.
Study trust and security: Learn the privacy and security controls described in the official exam material, including their limits.
Understand agent behavior: Review how topic classification, instructions, actions, and escalation work together.
Review Prompt Builder: Understand prompt template types, grounding choices, and how to test a prompt against its intended task.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers configuring and optimizing AI agents in Agentforce, including topic classification, prompt templates, guardrails, Data 360 grounding, and multi-channel deployment. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 72% pass mark, weighted towards AI Agents (35%) and Prompt Engineering (20%).

blocks.heading: Official credential and exam details
blocks.body: The [Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist Exam Guide](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005298924&language=en_US&type=1) lists 60 multiple-choice questions, up to five unscored questions, 105 minutes, a 72% passing score, and no prerequisite. Platform Administrator and Platform App Builder are recommended credentials, not requirements. The [Salesforce credential page](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/credentials/agentforcespecialist) describes the credential as managing and optimizing Agentforce. Check [Salesforce certification pricing](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005298916&language=en_US&type=1) before registering.

blocks.heading: Topics and Actions
blocks.body: Topics and actions are core parts of agent configuration in the official exam outline. Review how standard and custom topics describe the work an agent handles, and how actions let it perform specific tasks. Consider the agent security context and select an architecture that fits the business need.

blocks.heading: Instructions and Guardrails
blocks.body: Instructions guide the agent’s role, tone, and scope. Guardrails set boundaries on what it should not do. In a scenario, identify whether the requirement is asking for behavior guidance or a restriction, then configure the appropriate control.

blocks.heading: Einstein Trust Layer
blocks.body: The Einstein Trust Layer provides security and privacy services for Agentforce, but do not assume every form of data masking is enabled for every agent. Salesforce documents that pattern-based and field-based LLM masking is disabled for agents. Salesforce also documents zero data retention for information sent to third-party LLM providers; audit and feedback handling depends on the supported service and configuration. See Salesforce Help: [Trust and Agentforce](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.copilot_trust.htm&language=en_US&type=5), [Data Masking Limitations in Agentforce](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_trust_data_masking.htm&language=en_US), and [Agentforce (Default) Considerations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_default_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5).

blocks.heading: Data Grounding and Permissions
blocks.body: Agentforce can use Salesforce CRM data according to the permissions and security context that apply to the agent. Data 360 and Agentforce Data Libraries offer additional grounding options for configured sources, such as knowledge articles, fields, uploaded files, or web sources. These options are not required for every agent data access path. Choose a source that contains the information needed and confirm access is configured. See Salesforce Help: [The Building Blocks of Agents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_building_blocks.htm&language=en_US) and [Ground Agentforce in Data](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_parent_data.htm&language=en_US&type=5).

blocks.heading: Channels and Human Escalation
blocks.body: Agentforce can be deployed through supported channels such as Experience Cloud, web chat, Slack, and messaging. The Escalate to Agent standard action can hand a conversation to Omni-Channel for human routing. Learn which setup applies to the channel and when a handoff is appropriate.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Agentforce Specialist exam
scenarioTips.intro: Expect questions that describe a business need or an agent setup and ask you to choose a suitable configuration. Learn how the parts work together so you can explain why a design fits the scenario.

blocks.heading: Route requests to a topic and action
blocks.body: A topic describes the kinds of requests an agent should handle; its description helps guide classification. Actions perform work associated with a topic, such as invoking a flow, Apex, a prompt template, or a supported standard action. Choose the action based on the task the scenario requires.

blocks.heading: Apply Trust Layer controls carefully
blocks.body: Do not assume the Trust Layer masks personal information in every agent request. Salesforce documents that pattern-based and field-based masking are disabled for agents. Salesforce describes zero data retention for information sent to third-party LLM providers, while audit and feedback handling depends on service and configuration. These services support security and privacy but do not guarantee a generated answer is correct. Review [Agentforce masking limitations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_trust_data_masking.htm&language=en_US) and [Trust and Agentforce](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.copilot_trust.htm&language=en_US&type=5).

blocks.heading: Choose an appropriate grounding source
blocks.body: Prompt templates can use Salesforce record data through supported merge fields and grounding features. Data 360 can support broader grounding when the needed information comes from configured sources. Identify what data the response needs, where that data lives, and whether the agent has permission to use it.

blocks.heading: Plan channels and handoffs
blocks.body: When a scenario requires a human to take over, identify the supported escalation action and routing setup for that deployment. Check channel-specific configuration rather than assuming the same steps apply to every channel.

blocks.heading: Follow the current exam guide
blocks.body: Use the [official Salesforce exam guide](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005298924&language=en_US&type=1) for the latest objectives and format. Turn each objective into a practical review task, then revisit the areas where you need more practice.

nextCertsAfter.intro: You can build on Agentforce study with administrator, app-building, sales, or service credentials:

sampleQuestions.question: What is the main role of an Agentforce Specialist?
options: Configure, manage, and improve Agentforce agents
Write Apex code for agents
Design marketing campaigns
Set up CPQ products
sampleQuestions.explanation: Agentforce Specialists configure and improve agents using their knowledge of Salesforce and Agentforce.
whyWrong: Writing Apex is mainly a developer task.
Marketing campaign design is a Marketing Cloud task.
CPQ product setup is a separate area of expertise.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Topic in Agentforce?
options: A report category for dashboards
An area that tells an agent which requests to handle and what actions it can use
A Flow element that runs when a record is created
A permission set group for agent access
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Topic defines the kinds of requests an agent handles. It includes instructions and the actions the agent can use.
whyWrong: Reports and dashboards are not part of Topic setup.
A record-triggered Flow is a different automation feature.
Permission set groups control access, not which customer requests the agent handles.

sampleQuestions.question: What is an Agent Action?
options: A page layout for Agent Console
An email sent when a Case is escalated
A task an agent can perform, such as running a Flow, Apex, API, or Prompt Template
A Lightning Web Component in the chat window
sampleQuestions.explanation: Agent Actions are tasks an agent can perform. They can use Flows, Apex, external services, Prompt Templates, and standard Salesforce actions.
whyWrong: A page layout changes the user interface; it is not an action an agent performs.
An email sent on escalation is not an Agent Action.
A Lightning Web Component changes the interface; it is not a task the agent performs.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Salesforce capability gives Agentforce unified customer data?
options: Marketing Cloud Journeys
Commerce Cloud product catalog
Slack channels
Data 360
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data 360 provides unified customer profiles that Agentforce can use to add current customer context to responses.
whyWrong: Marketing Cloud Journeys manages marketing automation.
The Commerce Cloud catalog contains product data, not a unified customer profile.
Slack channels are for communication, not unified customer data.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Einstein Trust Layer do for Agentforce?
options: Protects customer data, applies privacy controls, and logs AI activity
Reports agent performance
Requires approval before every agent response
Uses a custom Flow to check every output
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Einstein Trust Layer protects customer data when Agentforce uses external large language models. It can mask sensitive data, prevent model providers from retaining data, and log AI activity for review.
whyWrong: Performance reports do not provide privacy and security controls.
Human approval for every answer is not what the Trust Layer does.
A custom Flow can check outputs, but it is separate from the Trust Layer.

sampleQuestions.question: What are Guardrails in an Agentforce agent?
options: Record security rules
Instructions for what the agent must not do
Limits on messages per hour
Rules for testing different agent versions
sampleQuestions.explanation: Guardrails tell the agent what not to do. They can help prevent off-topic replies, unauthorized promises, and harmful content.
whyWrong: Record security controls which records a user can see.
Message limits control system traffic, not agent behavior.
A/B testing compares agent versions; it does not set behavior limits.

sampleQuestions.question: Where can you deploy Agentforce agents for customer self-service?
options: Salesforce Service Console only
Slack and email only
Experience Cloud, web chat, and messaging channels such as SMS or WhatsApp
Salesforce mobile push notifications only
sampleQuestions.explanation: Agents can be deployed on Experience Cloud sites, web chat, and messaging channels so customers can get help without first reaching a person.
whyWrong: The internal Service Console alone does not provide customer self-service.
Agents can use channels beyond Slack and email.
Agents can use channels beyond mobile push notifications.

sampleQuestions.question: What is Prompt Builder used for in Agentforce?
options: Building Lightning Record Pages
Setting Omni-Channel routing rules
Writing Apex tests for custom actions
Creating reusable prompt templates that combine instructions with CRM or Data 360 data
sampleQuestions.explanation: Prompt Builder lets admins create prompt templates that combine instructions with live CRM data. These templates can support field generation, record summaries, sales emails, and agent actions.
whyWrong: Lightning Record Pages are built with Lightning App Builder.
Omni-Channel routing is a Service Cloud feature.
Apex tests are written by developers; Prompt Builder is a declarative tool.

sampleQuestions.question: How does an Agentforce agent choose a Topic for a customer message?
options: It uses a large language model to match the message to a Topic description and scope
It matches the Case category to a record type
The customer must select a Topic from a menu
It selects a Topic at random and escalates after two turns
sampleQuestions.explanation: The reasoning engine uses a large language model to identify the customer’s intent and choose a Topic based on its description and scope.
whyWrong: Matching a Case category to a record type is a rule-based approach, not the described intent matching.
Customers do not have to choose a Topic from a menu.
Topic selection is based on the request, not a random choice or fixed two-turn rule.

sampleQuestions.question: An agent gives incorrect or off-topic replies. What should the specialist do?
options: Delete and rebuild the agent
Review Topic instructions, Guardrails, and prompt grounding, then test different conversations
Add more Agent Actions
Increase the model temperature
sampleQuestions.explanation: Improve the Topic instructions, Guardrails, and prompt templates, then test a range of real conversation examples to find gaps.
whyWrong: Rebuilding discards the setup before you know what needs to change.
More actions do not fix unclear instructions or incorrect grounding.
A higher temperature adds variation and may make answers less reliable.

sampleQuestions.question: How can an Agentforce agent hand a conversation to a human service agent?
options: Use an Agent Escalation Flow
Use a Workflow Rule to create a Case when sentiment is negative
Use the standard Escalate to Agent action to send the conversation and context to Omni-Channel
Email the service team’s shared inbox
sampleQuestions.explanation: The standard escalation action transfers the conversation and its context to a human agent through Omni-Channel.
whyWrong: The built-in action is called Escalate to Agent.
A Workflow Rule may create a Case, but it does not hand over a live conversation.
An email alert does not transfer the live conversation and its context.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Agentforce Specialist exam mainly test?
options: Apex and Lightning Web Component development
Data 360 ingestion architecture
Service Cloud routing and Case classification
Configuring agents, including Topics, actions, prompts, Guardrails, channels, and Data 360
sampleQuestions.explanation: The exam tests how to configure agents: define Topics and actions, create prompt templates, use Guardrails, choose channels, and ground responses with Data 360.
whyWrong: Apex and Lightning Web Components are development topics, not the main focus of this exam.
Data 360 ingestion architecture is a separate architecture skill.
Omni-Channel routing and Case classification are Service Cloud topics.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Agentforce Guardrails?
options: Set limits on what the agent can do or say
Make replies more creative
Increase model temperature
Add more data sources
sampleQuestions.explanation: Guardrails set limits on the agent’s actions and responses.
whyWrong: Guardrails do not control how creative responses are.
Model temperature is a separate setting.
Guardrails do not add data sources.

sampleQuestions.question: Which action type can an Agentforce agent use to run a Flow?
options: Apex only
Flow action
External API only
Prompt Template only
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Flow is one of the standard action types an agent can use to perform tasks.
whyWrong: Agents can use more than Apex actions.
External APIs are a separate action type.
Prompt Templates are different from Flow actions.

sampleQuestions.question: When should you use Data 360 grounding for an Agentforce agent?
options: Never
Only for external channels
When the agent needs unified customer profiles and CRM data for its responses
Only while testing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data 360 grounding gives the agent access to unified customer data so it can provide responses based on that information.
whyWrong: Grounding is a common way to provide customer context.
Grounding is not limited to external channels.
Grounding can be used in production, not only in tests.

sampleQuestions.question: Before activating an agent for real users, how should a specialist confirm it behaves correctly across a range of scenarios?
options: Run it through Testing Center and review the evaluations
Deploy straight to production and watch for complaints
Ask the agent to describe its own instructions
Skip testing if the agent was built with a template
sampleQuestions.explanation: Testing Center runs an agent against defined test cases and scores its responses, so a specialist can catch problems before real users see them.
whyWrong: Deploying untested and waiting for complaints skips the verification step the exam expects.
Asking an agent to describe its own instructions doesn't verify its actual behavior across scenarios.
Templates still need testing, they aren't pre-verified for a specific org's data and configuration.

sampleQuestions.question: What's the difference between an Employee agent and a Service agent in Agentforce?
options: There is no difference, the terms are interchangeable
An Employee agent runs in the context of the logged-in internal user; a Service agent runs under a dedicated Agent User for external, customer-facing work
Employee agents can only use Flow actions, Service agents can only use Apex
Service agents cannot be tested in Testing Center
sampleQuestions.explanation: Employee agents act with the permissions of the internal user who's using them. Service agents, typically customer-facing, run under a separate Agent User whose permission sets define exactly what the agent can access.
whyWrong: They run under different security contexts, which is why the exam tests telling them apart.
Both agent types can use Flow, Apex, and other action types, the distinction isn't about which actions are available.
Testing Center works with both Employee and Service agents.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants two specialized agents, one for billing and one for technical support, to collaborate on a single complex customer request. Which concept addresses this?
options: A single Topic with more detailed instructions
Multi-Agent architecture, using open protocols such as MCP or A2A to orchestrate between agents
A bigger Guardrail
A longer prompt template
sampleQuestions.explanation: When a use case needs more scalability and control than one agent configuration can offer, Multi-Agent Orchestration lets separate agents work together, coordinated through protocols like Model Context Protocol (MCP) or Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication.
whyWrong: Adding instructions to one Topic doesn't give you two specialized, independently-governed agents working together.
Guardrails constrain what a single agent can say or do, they don't coordinate multiple agents.
A longer prompt template doesn't solve a multi-agent coordination problem.

sampleQuestions.question: An agent was built and tested in a sandbox. What should the specialist account for when moving it to production?
options: Nothing, agents deploy identically everywhere
Dependencies such as connected data sources, permission sets for the Agent User, and any environment-specific configuration
Only the agent's name needs to change
Production doesn't support Agentforce
sampleQuestions.explanation: Moving an agent from sandbox to production means checking that its grounding data sources, the Agent User's access, and any environment-specific settings all exist and are correctly configured in the target org.
whyWrong: Environments differ in data, access, and configuration, so deployment isn't a simple no-op copy.
A name change alone doesn't address the real dependencies a deployment needs to carry over.
Production is a normal, supported environment for Agentforce agents.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to prevent a specific large language model from being used by any agent in their org, for compliance reasons. Where is that controlled?
options: In the Topic's instructions
Through model access management in the Trust Layer
By deleting the Prompt Builder app
It can't be restricted, all models are always available
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Trust Layer includes model access management, letting admins allow or block specific models from being used across the org's agents and prompt templates.
whyWrong: Topic instructions shape agent behavior, they don't govern which underlying models are available org-wide.
Deleting Prompt Builder would break prompt template functionality entirely, it isn't a targeted model restriction.
Model access is specifically a governable setting through the Trust Layer, not an all-or-nothing default.
